### HANDLING MISSING DATA

```{r}
starwars %>%
  filter(is.na(hair_color)) %>% 
  print()
```

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  filter(is.na(sex)) %>%
  print()
```

We would like to replace to remove the ones whose gender is NA from our analysis.

```{r}
starwars %>%
  filter(!is.na(starwars$sex))
  print()
```

#### Changing Data Types in R

```{r}
glimpse(starwars)
```

**Changing the Character Formatted Columns into Categorical Format**

```{r}
as.factor(starwars$sex)
levels(sex)
```

### Data Imputation

```{r}
#first we would like to impute the hair color column but before that we would like to get the counts of each hair color
starwars %>% 
  select(hair_color) %>% 
  count(hair_color) %>% 
  print()
```

From this table we can see that the brown hair color was dominant among the different characters.

```{r}
# we would also like to see the number of the missing values in this column.
starwars %>% 
  select(hair_color) %>% 
  filter(is.na(hair_color)) %>% 
  count(hair_color) %>% 
  print()
```

We had 5 missing values in the column and hence it is expected that we would be imputing with brown.

```{r}
starwars %>%
  mutate(hair_color = case_when(is.na(hair_color) ~"brown",TRUE ~ hair_color)) %>% 
  print() %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header("Hair Color has been imputted in this dataset")

```

### Handling Numerical Columns with missing values

```{r}
ggplot(starwars,aes(x= mass))+
  geom_density(alpha=0.4,fill="maroon")+
  labs(title="Density Plot for the Mass Coloumn in the Starwars dataset")
```

Plotting a histogram for our dataset in the mass column

```{r}
ggplot(starwars,aes(x=mass))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 10,fill = "skyblue",alpha = 0.6)+
  labs(title="Histogram for the Mass column")
```

Our mass column is skewed towards the right hence we would use the median imputation instead

```{r}
#for this example I will be working with the mass coloumn
starwars %>%
  select(name,height,mass) %>% 
  mutate(mass = case_when(is.na(mass) ~ median(mass,na.rm = TRUE),TRUE ~ mass)) %>%
  print() %>%
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_nytimes() %>% 
  tab_header(title = "Mass Column Imputted by mean")
  
```

Now we can plot a violin plot for the mass column to also understand the distribution of the data

```{r}
ggplot(starwars,aes(y=mass))+
  geom_violin(fill="skyblue")+
  geom_boxplot(fill="blue")+
  theme_bw()
```

### Removing Missing Values

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  print() %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_theme_nytimes %>% 
  tab_header(title= "Starwars Dataset without any missing values")
```

### MUTATION OF FEATURES WITH R

```{r}
library('palmerpenguins')
data('penguins')
print(penguins)
```

```{r}
names(penguins)
```

We may want to change \~bill_length_mm into bill_length_cm which will be done by dividing the original feature by 10.

```{r}
penguins %>%
  drop_na() %>% 
  mutate(bill_length_cm = bill_length_mm/10)
```

#### Challenge

Convert the 'body_mass_g' into body_mass_kg by diving $$\frac{textbf{body_mass_g}}{1000}$$

```{r}
penguins %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass_g/1000) %>% 
  print()
```

### FILTERING

We may look to filter out the Penguin Species Adelie which belong to the male gender

```{r}
penguins %>% 
  filter((species == "Adelie") & (sex == "male")) %>% 
  arrange(-body_mass_g) %>% 
  print() %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_nytimes()
```

#### SUMMARIZING NUMERICAL DATA

```{r}
penguins %>%
  drop_na() %>% 
  select(species,bill_length_mm) %>% 
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarize(mean_bill_length = mean(bill_length_mm)) %>% 
  print() %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title = "Mean Bill Length mm per Species")
  
```

### **CATEGORICAL DATA ANALYSIS**

```{r}
library('forcats')
library('gapminder')
```

```{r}
data('diamonds')
print(diamonds)
```

```{r}
prop.table(table(diamonds$cut,diamonds$color))
```

```{r}
glimpse(diamonds)
```

```{r}
levels(diamonds$cut)
```

Combining Factors

```{r}
diamonds_1 <- diamonds %>% 
  mutate(cut = fct_collapse(cut,Good = c("Good","Ideal"),Better = c("Very Good"),Best = "Premium",medium = "Fair")) %>% 
  print()
```

How to change levels ordering in categorical data

```{r}
diamonds_1 %>% 
  mutate(cut = fct_drop(cut)) %>% 
  mutate(cut = fct_relevel(cut,c("Best","Better","Good","medium"))) %>%
  select(cut) %>% 
  table()
```

### Data Visualization

#### 1.Bar Graph

```{r}
diamonds_2 <- diamonds %>%
  select(cut) %>% 
  count(cut) %>% 
  print()
```

Visualizaing this in form of a bar graph

```{r}
ggplot(diamonds_2,aes(x= cut , y = n ,fill = cut))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity" , alpha = 0.5)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs( title = "Quality of Diamonds in quantity", x= "Category",y = "Count")
```
